content.text: Updated: Mar. 26, 2026, 8:10 p.m.Published: Mar. 26, 2026, 8:10 p.m.Back-to-back AL Manager of the Year Stephen Vogt leads the Cleveland Guardians into Seattle to open the season against the Mariners tonight. Find out how to watch for free.APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comSEATTLE – The Cleveland Guardians open the season against AL MVP runner-up Cal Raleigh and the Seattle Mariners tonight at T-Mobile Park. This game is available for free through multiple streaming servicesHow do I watch Guardians baseball for free today?This game will broadcast live on CleGuardians.TV and Mariners.TV at 10:10 p.m. Eastern. (7:10 p.m. Pacific). There are two ways to catch this game free. Fans who have parted ways with their local cable provider can watch at no cost by utilizing a free trial from DIRECTV, which also offers $35 off your first month. FuboTV has a free trial and $25 off your first month. All columns visible (no scrolling needed)Here are five storylines to watch for today’s game:1. An Opening Day clash between two reigning division winnersThe Guardians and Mariners face off tonight in the only season-opening game featuring two defending division champions looking to sustain their recent success. Both franchises made history in 2025, with Cleveland erasing a 15.5-game deficit to win the AL Central and Seattle ending a 24-year drought to capture the AL West title.2. Cleveland’s pursuit of offense after franchise-low hitting in 2025The Guardians are desperate to rejuvenate a lackluster offense that posted a franchise-low .226 batting average last season, ranking among the worst in major league baseball. The team is banking on cornerstones Jose Ramirez and Steven Kwan, while hoping to unleash rookie standout Chase DeLauter to provide the firepower necessary to support their reliable pitching staff.3. Seattle’s veteran core aims for a pennant following a historic runAfter falling just eight outs short of their first World Series appearance, the Mariners return with a powerful lineup featuring home run heavyweight Cal Raleigh, Randy Arozarena and former Guardian Josh Naylor. The team has solidified itself as a perennial pennant contender, boasting five All-Stars at the top of a batting order that pushed the Toronto Blue Jays to seven games in the ALCS. 4. A marquee pitching duel featuring Tanner Bibee and Logan GilbertCleveland starter Tanner Bibee looks to bounce back from a mediocre 2025 season against Seattle’s Logan Gilbert, who returns to form after missing nearly two months with a flexor strain. Both rotations are backed by high-leverage bullpens, though Cleveland begins the season without key reliever Hunter Gaddis due to a forearm injury. 5. A managerial homecomingGuardians’ manager Stephen Vogt returns to the Pacific Northwest for a homecoming of sorts, along with new coaches Tony Arnerich and Andy McKay. The matchup serves as a significant one for Vogt, an Olympia, Washington, resident who previously served as a bullpen coach for the Mariners. He is coming off his second consecutive AL Manager of the Year award.
